findings.title: Invalidate the connected-calendar query after deleting cache
findings.body: The delete mutation does not invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`; it only calls the optional `onSuccess` prop, which may be undefined. After deletion, the cached query can continue returning the old `cacheUpdatedAt`, so the dropdown still reports cache data and offers deletion until the query is otherwise refreshed. Invalidate the query on successful deletion (or ensure the callback always refreshes it).

findings.title: Exclude expired cache rows from cache status
findings.body: This status query groups every row for the credential without filtering `expiresAt`. Expired rows are ignored by `getCachedAvailability`, but remain in the database, so they can cause the UI to show a last-updated timestamp and a delete action even when no cache entry can be served. Filter to unexpired rows if this status is meant to represent usable cached data.

findings.title: Resolve the env file path independently of the caller's working directory
findings.body: `ENV_FILE` is relative to the current working directory, not this script's location. Running the script from the repository root (for example, `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`) reads or creates `../.env` instead of the repository's `.env`, so the app does not receive the configured webhook URL. Resolve the path from the script directory or set it explicitly.

findings.title: Use a sed in-place-edit form that works on Linux
findings.body: `sed -i ''` is the BSD/macOS form for an in-place edit and fails with GNU sed, commonly used in Linux development and CI environments. When `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` already exists, the script therefore cannot update the env file on those systems. Use a portable edit strategy or branch for the platform.
